description: Network topology of all 15 HFT platform services. Edges represent runtime dependencies (caller -> callee). Finalized 2026-09-11 (Phase 2, item 4): every upstream/downstream array is re-derived from edges[] (see direction-convention note) and cross-checked against the client code on disk.

services.name: market-data-gateway
services.description: Ingests raw venue feeds (ITCH/FIX/MDP3), normalizes to canonical wire format, maintains sequence tracking and quality metrics, distributes quotes to downstream consumers.

services.name: order-book-builder
services.description: Maintains L2 limit order books per (symbol, venue) from normalized quotes. Computes top-of-book, detects material changes (spread moves, imbalance, depth drain), emits book events to subscribers.

services.name: strategy-engine
services.description: Consumes book events and quotes to generate trading signals (entry/exit). Runs pluggable strategy modules (momentum, mean-reversion, spread arbitrage). Emits order intents to the execution gateway.

services.name: execution-gateway
services.description: Translates order intents from the strategy engine into venue-specific order messages (FIX/ITCH). Manages order lifecycle (new, modify, cancel, replace), tracks acknowledgments, and reports fill events back. Makes no outbound calls of its own: order intents are pushed to it (POST /orders) and consumers poll it (GET /fills) — see the S13 design-intent note.

services.name: risk-manager
services.description: Pre-trade and real-time risk checks. Enforces position limits, notional caps, velocity limits, kill-switch triggers. Veto power over the execution gateway (can reject or flatten).

services.name: position-keeper
services.description: Maintains authoritative real-time position state per (account, symbol). Applies fills, corporate actions, and manual adjustments. Provides position snapshots for analytics and settlement.

services.name: latency-monitor
services.description: Measures and reports end-to-end latency across the pipeline: venue-to-gateway, gateway-to-book, book-to-signal, signal-to-order, order-to-ack. Maintains rolling percentiles (p50/p99/p999) and fires alerts on budget breaches. Pure push-based service: it exposes POST /stamp (pipeline stages POST the timestamp pair or a pre-computed duration) and keeps an in-memory, per-stage, budget-bounded alert history; it makes no outbound calls itself (no upstream edges).

services.name: data-quality-monitor
services.description: Aggregates quality metrics from S1 (staleness, gaps, ordering violations) and S2 (book health, cross events). Produces a unified data-quality dashboard view and triggers degradation alerts.

services.name: portfolio-analytics
services.description: Computes P&L (realized/unrealized), Sharpe ratio, drawdown, VaR, and attribution analytics from positions + fills. Serves historical and real-time portfolio metrics to the API gateway.

services.name: alerting-service
services.description: Central alert aggregation, deduplication/suppression, escalation and acknowledgement tracking. Receives alerts from risk-manager (S5), latency-monitor (S7) and data-quality-monitor (S8); collapses repeated occurrences into logical alerts, escalates un-acknowledged WARNINGs to CRITICAL and flags aged CRITICALs for on-call.

services.name: config-service
services.description: Centralized configuration store and distribution. Serves versioned config blobs to all services at boot and on change (long-poll). Manages environment overrides and feature flags. Ships AlertingClient (S10) and AuditClient (S13) for best-effort fan-out; no service on disk issues a config-service client call, so it has no caller edges — see the design-intent note.

services.name: auth-service
services.description: Authentication and authorization. Issues and validates JWT tokens for inter-service and external API calls. Manages service-to-service mTLS certificates and API key rotation.

services.name: audit-logger
services.description: Immutable append-only audit trail for trading actions: risk vetoes and kill-switch activations (S5) and config changes (S11) are the code-backed sources today; order-lifecycle submissions (S4) are the documented design intent. Provides tamper-evident hash-chained log with query API.

services.name: settlement-service
services.description: End-of-day and intra-day settlement reconciliation. Idempotently settles fills per settlement date, matches them against venue statements (quantity/price tolerances), computes net positions and cash roll-ups, flags discrepancies, and seals each day with a tamper-evident SHA-256 content hash. Ingests S6 position snapshots into today's run.

services.name: api-gateway
services.description: External-facing REST API gateway. Authenticates every non-local request by validating the bearer token against auth-service (POST /verify) and authorizing the route against the token's read/write scopes, then reverse-proxies /settlement/** to settlement-service and /portfolio/** to portfolio-analytics, rewriting the path (stripping the gateway prefix) and passing through the upstream's status and body verbatim. Top of the call graph: it exposes /settlement/** and /portfolio/** but no other service calls it.

edges.description: Order book builder subscribes to normalized quotes from gateway
Strategy engine consumes raw quotes for signal computation
Strategy engine subscribes to book events (TOP_CHANGE, SPREAD_CHANGE, etc.)
Strategy engine pushes order intents (POST /orders) to the execution gateway
Risk manager queries book top-of-book state for pre-trade reference prices
Risk manager reads open orders/fills and can cancel/flatten via the execution gateway
Risk manager POSTs breach / kill-switch alerts to the alerting service (fire-and-forget)
Risk manager POSTs risk vetoes and kill-switch activations to the audit logger
Position keeper polls /fills from the execution gateway and applies each fill exactly once
Position keeper pulls top-of-book mids for mark-to-market reference prices in snapshots
Data quality monitor pulls quality metrics from gateway (/quality)
Data quality monitor pulls book health and cross events (/books)
Data quality monitor POSTs degradation alerts to the alerting service (fire-and-forget)
Portfolio analytics polls /positions from position-keeper for P&L computation
Config service POSTs a WARNING alert to the alerting service on store anomalies (best-effort)
Config service POSTs config-change events to the audit logger (best-effort)
Settlement service queries positions for EOD reconciliation (background ingest loop)
API gateway proxies GET /portfolio/pnl|metrics|var|attribution|history to portfolio-analytics (path rewritten, query forwarded, bodyless)
API gateway validates every bearer token via POST /verify; readyz polls GET /healthz
API gateway proxies POST /settlement/settle|finalize|ingest + GET /settlement/reports|runs|discrepancies to settlement-service (path rewritten, query forwarded)

notes: All edges use HTTP/JSON (no gRPC, no message queue) per platform constraint.
Streaming edges use chunked JSON-lines over a single long-lived GET connection.

Direction convention (2026-09-11, final): edges[] are the CANONICAL source of truth. Each edge {from:A, to:B} means A calls B (A opens the connection; A is caller/client, B callee/server). For every service: upstream = { to : edge.from == service } (the services it CALLS) and downstream = { from : edge.to == service } (the services that CALL IT). Every entry of every upstream/downstream array is backed by exactly one edge and vice versa; the 2026-09-11 (item 4) reconciliation re-derived all 15 services' arrays from edges[] and corrected: S4 (upstream [S3] had no edge, because S3 pushes intents TO S4 — now downstream [S3,S5,S6], upstream []), S5 (upstream [S2,S4,S10,S13] matches its clients exactly), S7 (removed phantom upstream [S1..S4] and downstream [S10] — it is purely push-based, POST /stamp, and makes no outbound calls), S8 (added missing S10 in upstream), S9/S14 (downstream [S15] — the API gateway proxies to them), S13 (removed phantom upstream [S4,S11,S12]; its real callers are S5 and S11), and S11 (upstream [S10, S13] for its best-effort alerting + audit fan-out). S10's callers are the three code-backed sources that POST alerts: S5, S8 and S11.

S11 config-service: by design it is the intended boot-time configuration source for all 15 services (config-service long-poll discovery was adopted before the current hard-coded-URL pattern in CONVENTIONS §5/§11), but NO service on disk currently issues a config-service client call — no service ships a cfgs URL, and deploy/env.example documents zero functional env overrides from S11. S11's caller list is therefore documented as design intent and is intentionally NOT represented in edges[]; it is the single documented exception to the edge-backing rule above. Only when a real cfgs client is added should the 14 intended consumers be re-derived into edges[] and S11's downstream array.

S13 audit-logger: the documented audit sources are S4 (order lifecycle), S5 (vetoes, kill-switch), S11 (config changes) and S12 (token lifecycle). Only S5 and S11 ship audit clients on disk (rkm AuditClient, cfgs AuditClient), which is why S13.downstream == [S5, S11] and only those two edges exist; the S4 and S12 submissions are documented design intent with no client code today. When such a client is added, add its edge and re-derive S13.downstream.

deploy/docker-compose.yml depends_on blocks reflect the edge graph as startup ordering, with two documented deviations from the code-backed upstream sets: (a) S10/S13 are added where a service has them as best-effort sinks for boot order (e.g. S8 on S1/S2/S10), and (b) risk-manager (S5) additionally depends_on strategy-engine (S3) even though no S5->S3 client exists on disk — S3 is present purely for startup ordering (signals should be flowing before risk checks go live), and it is deliberately NOT an edge.
